utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes. Can you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number, IT-99-36-T, is Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin and Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, good morning to you. Can you hear me in a language that -- THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I can hear you and I understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner, assisted by Susan Grogan case manager this morning replacing Denise Gustin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you both. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Milan Trbojevic. My assistant is Ms. Jevtovic for Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And appearances for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic and Natasha Ivanovic-Fauveau for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we have his consent, obviously, for today's sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So are there any preliminaries before we bring the witness in? Okay. So usher -- where is the usher. He is already -- he has already gone.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The only thing is, Your Honour, I obviously haven't been able to speak -- I wasn't even aware whether he'd arrived or not. I'm told he has. It may be that Your Honour wants to explain if he hasn't already heard where General Talic is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Definitely I will, Ms. Korner. Thank you for reminding me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Filipovic, and welcome back to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- this Tribunal. You are familiar with the procedure. I don't need to explain it again to you. Please proceed with making the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before we proceed with the cross-examination, let me explain two very simple matters, two things. First of all, you remember that the last time you were sitting on that chair I explained to you why we had to cancel one sitting or start very late. The reason was that General Talic had to be admitted to hospital at the same time. We didn't even know that you were just being discharged from hospital, where you had been for some treatment. The position resulted ultimately to be one of much -- much more serious than we had anticipated or we had an idea of at the time. General Talic is seriously ill, and we've spent the last two weeks trying to find out how best to deal with him and also to proceed with this case without prejudicing the course of the trial. We have agreed -- or we have decided to separate the two accused, so this trial is going to continue against Mr. Brdjanin, and the trial against General Talic will resume -- will continue if and when he is physically fit to continue. But for the purpose of your evidence, your testimony, since you had already started giving evidence and finished the examination-in-chief and started already -- we were halfway through the first of the two cross-examinations, it -- there was an agreement between the Defence team for General Talic, the Prosecution, and also the Defence team for Brdjanin that you will continue -- you will proceed with your cross-examination, with your testimony, with General Talic still being in this case. He will disappear from this case as soon as you finish your testimony. But until you finish your testimony, he is in this case. He can't be with us because he is sick. He is ill. And he is not in a position to appear before any Tribunal for the time being. But he has given his consent for you to -- and for you to continue giving evidence and for us to continue hearing your evidence in his absence. So that's what's going to happen today. Also, Mr. Ackerman is not with us today, and the cross-examination which he had started will be continued by -- proceeded with by Mr. Trbojevic. And after that, Mr. Zecevic or Madam Fauveau, on behalf of General Talic, will proceed with their cross-examination for General Talic. Have I made myself clear to you? Do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. But the only thing I would like to say is that I can't hear that well. The earphones don't seem to be perfect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The last thing obviously is it's -- it's incumbent on me as President of this Trial Chamber to express our regret and offer our apologies for any inconvenience all this may have caused to you. We realised that there were days where you had to wait endless hours, and this was no fun at all, and I am sure it brought you some discomfort and some inconvenience, for which we are sorry and please accept our apologies. Hopefully by Friday at the latest all this will be over and you should be able to return back to your country. I thank you. Mr. Trbojevic. Incidentally, even my earphones -- it's as if there is a continuous or recurring short-circuit somewhere. No, no. It's not a question of volume. It's a question of -- we can proceed. I don't want to stop. But I do have these interferences more or less -- thank you. Mr. Trbojevic, you don't need to introduce yourself or anything. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: When you started giving testimony, on one occasion you said that you had been informed that Mr. Brdjanin -- you said he requested a structure of the government in the municipality. Could you explain this, please. What does it refer to?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say exactly how this happened. All I can say is that he came around 1991. I don't know the exact date. I know that at that time a document that had been signed by Mr. Brdjanin arrived, and in that document he was wondering how the SDS would establish power, would set up power. We didn't have that document. We weren't able to see that document, but we found out that this had arrived through people who were aware of these things in the world. And as events unfolded, on the basis of the events, I -- it's my opinion that it said that the SDS should keep the police in that document, the Secretariat of National Defence, the tax -- inland revenue, the post office. So it was necessary to divide power after the first multi-party elections. So I assume that it referred to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: So that could have been at the beginning of 1991, when power was established in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From halfway through that year. I don't know the exact date, but I know it was in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: The elections were in 1990.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please slow down and make a pause between the question and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Trbojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, the usual problem when both of you are speaking Serbo-Croat: You don't give each other a chance, a pause before one proceeds with the question or one proceeds with the answer. The interpreters need a pause each time one of you starts speaking. Okay? And slow down, both of you, please. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not going ask you in more detail about that document, since, as you say, you haven't seen it. But my client has asked me to deny that claim because he says that he never signed such a document.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's your problem and the problem of your client. You have the right to claim whatever you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: We won't go into a dispute. This is going to be the Prosecution's affair. The Prosecution will have to prove this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Similarly, at the beginning of your testimony -- it's page 9392 of the transcript -- you mentioned the barracks in Laniste.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: For the Knin Corps. And in that context, you claimed that it was on the authorisation of the organs of the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain what the basis for this claim is.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can explain to you is by putting a question to you. Mr. Ackerman preceded you, so someone must have told you about this four-storey building without anyone's authorisation cannot be constructed. And Kljuc, as a town, is not rich enough to construct such a building, so someone must have authorised it. It must have come from the top levels and the resources must have been secured.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: I can't answer your question. I'm not allowed to answer your question. But I would like to draw your attention to the fact that when you say someone had to authorise this, why should that someone be the Autonomous Region of Krajina, since permits for construction would be issued in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That building didn't have a permit for construction, and there was no authorisation. That building was built illegally, let's say. It hadn't been authorised. And believe me, the resources for the construction of that building didn't come from Sarajevo nor from Zagreb. They could only have come from Banja Luka or from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please -- you're doing the same thing that Mr. Trbojevic has been doing. When he finishes his question, allow just a couple of seconds before you start answering the -- giving your answer, because otherwise, the interpreters will have a difficulty. I mean, I can -- I can see how difficult it is for them already to keep pace with you, with the speed of the exchange of question and answer that is going on. Slow down, both of you, please. Yes, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: In the statement that you gave on the 24th of May, 1997 to the investigators of the Prosecution, you said that at a meeting your brother thanked the Serbs for having organised themselves politically because that provided the opportunity to the Bosniaks. That's what you said more or less.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That wasn't just at some meeting. That was on the founding Assembly of the SDS in Kljuc. And Radovan Karadzic was present at that same meeting. That was on the terrace of the Lana restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. But on the basis of this, at that time the Bosniaks had not organised themselves politically yet.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bosniaks were politically organised but you yourself were well aware of the times we were living in. It was necessary for someone to make the first move. We allowed the Serbs to do that because the Serbs --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. You also explained that you were in favour of the Municipality of Kljuc entering the community of Municipalities of Bosnian Krajina but you weren't in favour of it entering the Autonomous Region of Krajina, and the reasons you provided were that that would mean Serb domination, Orthodox domination, the use of the Cyrillic script, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Because that first region is one thing, the region of the Municipalities of Bosnian Krajina. And the Autonomous Region of Bosnian Krajina is another thing, because we knew that -- we knew what the first thing was and we knew what the second thing was, because earlier on we were in the Jajce region and it was all the same to us whether we would be in the Jajce region, the Banja Luka region, the Prijedor region. It was all the same to us. But as far as the Autonomous Region of Bosnian Krajina is concerned in which the Serbs were expected to be the dominant people and the Cyrillic script was to be in use and the religion was to be the Orthodox religion, as far as this is concerned, as far as all this being in the first place, we were against that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: But the territory of the Autonomous Region is the same as the Municipality of Banja Luka, the region of the Communities of Municipalities in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the say. In geographical terms, it's the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: The same people.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you completely, in geographical terms, in terms of the people, yes, it's the same. But in the first territory, there would be both Bosniaks and Croats, and in the Autonomous Region there were only the Serbs, regardless of the fact that in geographical terms the territory was the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Did someone express this or put it down on paper?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was well known. It was well known, because from Kljuc there were no delegates from Kljuc in the Autonomous Region of Bosnian Krajina. There were no Muslims or Croats, no Muslim or Croat delegates, only Serbs, whereas in the other region there were both Muslims and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to ask a question. I have no copies, but this is the title of an article and later this will be evidence for the Defence, and it shall later on be translated. May I do this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] You've had two weeks -- no. I won't allow you to do that. If you haven't circulated it before, there is no justification -- I see no reason why you should bring this document out now at the eleventh hour, surprising everyone. Forget the witness, because the witness has no right to see the documents beforehand. But the Prosecution -- at least the Prosecution should know what document we're talking about. I mean, they have facilities to have it translated to them, but -- we're talking of a document which we don't understand, I don't understand, the Prosecution doesn't understand, my colleagues don't understand, and you're handing -- you expect to hand it over to the witness, ask questions on it, without copies being available here and now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have it -- have it photocopied. Have it distributed in good time. And then towards the end of your cross-examination perhaps you would -- we would be in a position to allow you to put the question. But not like this. No, definitely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much. All I wanted was to read a title which consists of five words and ask whether the gentleman here wrote this down, nothing else. And all of these other things, I would have done them subsequently, of course. But I shall do as you said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you said that your brother was buried in a graveyard. Some other witnesses mentioned the Sehidsko graveyard. Could you translate this for us and tell us what language it's in.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will ask you where. Where was he buried?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: You said your brother was buried in Banja Luka, that the wives were present, his wife and Ivan Bender's wife, that they were taken then to the graveyard in Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was buried in the graveyard in Banja Luka. I have a certificate about my brother's death.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: That's not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, because in -- according to one story, he died of a natural death, but the doctor established that he had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: This is not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me bring you both to order, because you're running off at a tangent, both of you. The question that was put to you and which I would like you to answer is -- was this: In your statement, you said that your brother was buried in a graveyard. Some other witnesses mentioned the Sehidsko graveyard. Could you translate this for us. Tell us what language it's in. What does the word "Sehidsko" mean to you? First of all, what language is that, does that word belong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That means, if we translate it into your language -- Mezarje is a cemetery for citizens of merit, citizens who have merited of certain privileges in that society. And because of this, they have a special grave. For example, in a given state, the Queen will be buried in a special place, the Prime Minister, et cetera, will have a special grave. So the Sehidsko Mezarje in the Bosnian language means cemetery for people who have merited something more than other citizens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this is a purely etymologically Bosnian word, a Bosnian word.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I don't think it is necessary to proceed with questions on who was present during the exhumation and --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, it's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So you got your answer and perhaps you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to know which language these words came from.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably from Turkish. These are words that were appropriated by the Bosnian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: That's all I wanted to know; nothing else. You said that the Crisis Staff, of which you and your brother were a member, was formed in the second half of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Could we conclude that that was one of the first Crisis Staffs in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: But it's not in dispute that in 1991 this preceded the Crisis Staffs which were founded in 1992. You mentioned the adoption of a decision on the foundation of the Bosnian Municipality of Kljuc. As far as I have understood, that also took place in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I would just like to correct you. It wasn't the Bosniak, but the Bosnian Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And that was before the decision was adopted on proclaiming the Serbian Municipality of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbs de facto proclaimed it, but it wasn't on paper. But from the first multi-party elections onwards, the Serbs in Kljuc formed the Serbian Municipality of Kljuc, but it hadn't been put down on paper because everything was under the sign of the Serbs and the SDS as of 1990, from the time we split.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: But in that municipality in 1991 you participated in this.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we participated in it. And to a large extent we always left sessions when an agenda would be imposed that didn't suit us, but yes, you could say that in terms of the documents that exist, we made the first move and we were the first ones to proclaim the Bosnian Municipality of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: And you formed the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: And the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the witness to be shown the exhibit of the Prosecution P877.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: I would like you to pay attention to the last paragraph on page 1 and the first two lines on page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Trbojevic, can you read them in your language so that at least we can follow -- we can have them translated and we can follow, because we can only -- only look at the version in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. This is a letter by the SDS in Kljuc, dated 26th of February, 1992, and it is addressed to the SDS, Serbian Democratic Party of BH, and is about the election of judges in the municipality of Kljuc. Here it is alleged that during the division of power in the municipality, the position of the president of the court was given to the SDA, Party of Democratic Action. So the position of the president of the court was given to the SDA, which at the time when this letter was written was there, and so it says "In addition to the president of the court, another judge of Muslim nationality is currently working at the court. So the appointment of additional two judges of Muslim nationality to this important state organ would completely disrupt ethnic equality."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's your question, Mr. Trbojevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more sentence, please, I'd like to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: "For this reason, we propose that only one judge of Muslim nationality be appointed to the basic court." And my question to the witness: Is that correct that the president of the court was a Muslim, a Bosniak?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the name. Did any one of you mention a name?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not interested in a name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that the president -- that the president of the Court was Dzemal Botenic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct that there was a proposal to elect a further two judges?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't a proposal, but there was a competition. There was an advertisement for two vacant posts of judges. And among others, as far as I know, Nihad Filipovic also applied, and the judges were supposed to be appointed by the Assembly of BH. So what they did was they replied to the advertisement. And as far as I know, one of these people who applied was Nihad Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. That's enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't need that exhibit any more. I would like the witness to be shown the Prosecution Exhibit P878. Your Honour, in the English version it's on the first page beneath the agenda, in the first paragraph of the agenda. It starts with: "Briefing by Veljko Kondic." And then what's been said is that the Prime Minister Designate is Nikola Erceg. I'd like the witness to have a look at the text which is below the agenda, under 81. If he can read. It's quite difficult to read, under B.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: "The Assembly of the AP of Banja Luka was held, where there were opinions that the Republic of Bosnian Krajina should be formed, but it was understood that this was not the time for that. He then talked about the conference regarding BH and cantonisation. All revenues would belong to the region. The national bank would be based in Banja Luka. The Prime Minister Designate Nikola Erceg was elected," and so on. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Incidentally, for the record, Ms. Korner, I hope that the correct word was cantonisation, because in the English version it is "cannonisation," and I think we are far from having reached that stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said "cantonisation."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: I have a question for you.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Someone is reporting here to Veljko Kondic at the session of the executive board of the municipal board of the SDS. It can be seen here from the header. Did you know about the session in Banja Luka on the 6th of March, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Just a moment. Did Mr. Trbojevic say reporting to Veljko Kondic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Because my understanding -- I'm just wondering if that is a mistranslation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know, but that's what I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It is reporting by Mr. Kondic to the Crisis Staff -- or to the -- sorry, to the municipal board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Trbojevic. You've heard what Ms. Korner has just stated. The translation that we had was someone is reporting here to Veljko Kondic. Is it someone is here reporting to Veljko Kondic or someone -- or Veljko Kondic is reporting to someone? What did you actually state?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I read, as it said in the minutes, and it says that Veljko Kondic is the one reporting at the session of the executive board. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So that goes down for the record. Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: So what I'm asking the witness is did they know about this meeting and these discussions?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know specifically about this meeting, but I can tell the Chamber that there wasn't a day that went by that the representatives went to Banja Luka for a meeting. But I don't know specifically about this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm more interested whether was this known. Were there talks about these plans that the Krajina ARK should have a bank in Banja Luka that would be based in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was known. I said that in my previous testimony. That means, financial means were directed in that direction to Banja Luka through the public accounting service. So if I pay tax, me as a citizen, the tax would not go to Sarajevo. It would go to Banja Luka. So all the financial means through the SDK, the public accounting service, would be going to Banja Luka. But specifically about this meeting, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Could I ask you to check whether in these minutes, could you please check that there is no mention of Radoslav Brdjanin here in any context.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's no need for the witness to check that, quite honestly. If there was mention, it would be in the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... agrees that there's no mention of your client in this document. So next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: We'll go back to 1991. You mentioned helicopters that were distributing weapons around villages. So I have to ask you whether you were an eyewitness of this.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw helicopters flying. I saw helicopters landing. But I was not there, so that I can say that a helicopter landed. But people did come to me and say, "A helicopter landed in the village of Ljubine and they were unloading something," and I did see helicopters. A helicopter is not a fly so that you fail to see it. A helicopter would fly and then suddenly it would land. All the helicopters were olive-drab colour, so these were military helicopters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like the witness to be shown P880.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm interested at the bottom of the page, and I will tell you exactly. The last third of the page, I think that this is Djuro Trninic, if I can say.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's Djuro Trninic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: It says: There are not many weapons or ammunition. And this is again the session of the executive board of the SDS. And at the end of the page, Djuro Trninic says there is a lack of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is Dragan Babic. As far as I can see, that's Drago Djukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: In the very last sentence, it says there is a shortage of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: It's Drago Djukic.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: And on the second page, there is a name, Milenko Mackic is saying there is a lack of weapons. Do you agree with me that it says that here?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: And that's 12th of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't need the exhibit any more. I would like to ask that the witness be shown Exhibit P882.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'd like to ask something, if I may. The counsel is now finding some documents where I'm just supposed to confirm what it says, what is written. But when they had their sessions, when they held their sessions, they could have written anything. It says here what they did in minutes, but they could have said there's a lack of weapons. Maybe they needed weapons to arm a battalion and they had enough for a company. So I'm just wondering. These are minutes from sessions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's perfectly legitimate. I mean, it's difficult for me to -- to explain all this to you, but it is a perfectly regular question. You are being shown a document, and you're just being asked to confirm that the particular document does contain this -- this or that particular statement. That's all. You're not being asked to comment on the merits of what is contained -- or what is stated in that document. So don't worry about it. Just answer the question. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Although, Your Honour, actually what's happening is not really cross-examination at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know. But what is the alternative, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Because particularly with the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. I've been thinking about that all along since we started. What's the alternative? You tell me what's the alternative is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The alternative is Mr. Trbojevic puts questions which challenge what the witness has said, if that's what his case is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think Mr. Trbojevic knows exactly what he should be doing. Anyway, please proceed, Mr. Trbojevic, and try to ask questions that are of utility or which goes straight to the heart of the case of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness is claiming that Serb villages were armed, and I'm showing a document where it says that there was a lack of weapons, that there was a shortage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But Mr. Trbojevic, the same exhibit that you have just referred to, Exhibit P880, towards the very end of it there's Veljko Kondic, who is reported here, at least on this document, without prejudice to the authenticity of otherwise of this document, because I wouldn't like to comment about that, but it says "We will undertake to get additional weapons. I have no note that not everything is finished yet. We have to start keeping records immediately. All documents are to be brought by the next meeting." So -- do you want a confirmation of this from -- from the gentleman in the witness stand? I mean, come on. Let's -- let's go straight -- this is why I'm telling you lest -- I'm not in the habit of stopping anyone. As much as I can, I try to avoid that. But on the other hand, a cross-examination is a cross-examination. Let's get it over and done with.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to ask that the witness be shown Exhibit P882, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: You have already seen this document. This is a report of the 13th Partisan Brigade, dated 23rd of March, 1992. On page 2 there is an assessment. It's about halfway on the page, that in the areas of responsibility that there are many paramilitary formations, and for the Kljuc municipality it says that there are two companies in Kljuc; in Sanica, there's one battalion; in Krasulje, there are two companies. In your testimony, you said this was not true, and I'd like to ask you whether it was possible that it is completely untrue. Is it completely untrue that these formations were not there?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still claim this is not true, because this is the document in the time period the beginning of 1992 when all officers who were Muslims and Croats were taken out, taken off. I used to be a captain in the brigade. At that time we were all stopped being officers. And at the meeting I said, "Why are only Muslims and Croats being demoted? Why have they stopped being officers? Why is not Vinko Kondic being stopped from being an officer?" And I am saying that this is not at all true that the municipality of Kljuc had two companies, that Sanica had one battalion, if Krasulje had two companies. If this was true, then we would never have been expelled from Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask that the witness be shown Defence Exhibit DB96. 96, please. And a copy for the witness, please. The witness doesn't have a copy. Do you have a statement in our language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Chuqing, please. Because we are wasting time.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I think the witness already had a copy in front of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. Give it to him and let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: This is a statement by Ismet Muratagic dated 25th of June, 1992. You don't have to read it all. Do you know Ismet Muratagic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: In his statement he said that he led a group --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you -- Mr. Trbojevic, if you're going to ask any question to the witness referring to any particular part of this document, then please tell us which part, so that he's given the opportunity to read it before you put the question. And depending on the question, I may have to decide to give him the opportunity to read the whole document, if that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked the witness whether he knew the man who had given this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. But that's not what -- that's not what I asked you. I asked you if you are going to refer to any particular paragraph, then please indicate the paragraph to the witness so -- and to us so that we go straight to that paragraph. In the meantime, perhaps Mr. Filipovic, you can answer the question do you know Ismet Muratagic. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I answered affirmatively. Yes, I do know him. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: On page 2 of this statement, the witness said that he was at a meeting where the witness and his brother also attended, Asim Egrlic, Ibrahim Egrlic and many others. That's not important. Could you confirm that this is true?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: You said true?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: I will also ask you to look on page 4, on the second paragraph in which the person is describing a certain event. And he said, "I returned again to the position, to the village of Bajrami, and at about 10.00 hours, an official police car came, and behind it there was a white van and they stopped before the barricade. At the moment when the cars -- the vehicles were being stopped and started to get out of them, fire was opened on them from the positions without anyone giving an order, and so he describes the firing -- the shooting. And at the end of the paragraph, he says -- in the last three lines, he says: "I noticed that by the roadside several metres behind the police vehicle there was a body of a policeman that was lying down, while the others weren't around," and so on. In relation to the same incident, on the next page, it says -- and this is top of the page -- that "Looking for those people who have scattered, they found wounded Zeljko Despot." Have you found that part?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Despot Zeljko.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: In the -- at the top of the page. At the top of this page.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can we proceed with the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: The question that I want to put to the witness is: Do you know anything about this event?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about this event. All I know is that I think that on the 27th of May this conflict broke out. That's all I know. And I also know that, because Vinko insisted, because men from Krasulje wouldn't allow the body of Dusan to be taken out. So Vinko asked for Omer because they said that no one could approach without Omer's permission. And I know that Omer and Vinko went there together then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Was this Despot wounded? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know is what happened to Dusan Stojakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We won't be needing this document any longer. Could you now show the witness Defence Exhibit DB95.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Is this an order from the MUP, the Ministry of the Interior, in Bosnia and Herzegovina dated the 29th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it appears to be so. But it should have a signature and a stamp. Anyone could have typed this. But I think it is because --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Was the minister the minister at the time?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But for a document to be valid, it needs a signature and a stamp. But I think it is correct. I have no idea though.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: It says "I order," under 1. "Totally obstruct all roads in the territory of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in which units of the former JNA have started pulling out materiel and equipment." Under item 2: "Larger areas with military installations from which they are trying to pull out materiel and equipment are to be blocked," et cetera, et cetera. Under item 3: "Unannounced convoys of former JNA units and convoys without MUP escort shall not be allowed to leave the barracks or to communicate within the territory of the Republic of BH." And under item 4, it says: "The planning and launching of combat activities throughout the territory of the Republic of BH is to be accelerated and these activities are to be coordinated with the Territorial Defence staffs of the region, district, and the Republic of BH." And it's been signed by the minister, Alija Delimustafic. And the date was the 29th of April, 1992. Is that what it says, sir?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't need this document any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Here Mr. Trbojevic, I need to censor you, because this is not the way to deal with such an item or such a matter in -- upon cross-examination. I mean, it's -- we don't need the witness to tell us that this document says what you have read out. We just have to refer to the document, read it, and that's it. I mean, if anything, you ask the witness whether he can confirm whether he is -- was aware of this document, whether he's seen it before, whether he has anything to state about it, but not whether it says what you have read. I mean, you don't need the witness to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right, Your Honour. I should have asked the witness whether he had received this order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or rather, whether this order arrived in the Crisis Staff of which he was a member.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a question for me, is it? As I said earlier on in my testimony, we didn't receive that order. The first time I saw that order was ten days ago here in The Hague. I'm not saying that this order wasn't sent somewhere, but we in Kljuc did not receive it. We weren't able to get it. With regard to the 29th of April, at that time in Kljuc we were practically under SDS occupation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness denies that he is familiar with this. I have -- I can't ask him any further questions about this document now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: We'll now return to your testimony, according to which Bosniak policemen refused to sign a pledge of loyalty for the new police force. You said something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 889.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: This is a document which was signed by Milos on the 24th of April, 1992. Were you aware of someone who used the pseudonym Milos?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether this is a pseudonym. It could be the person's name, because there are several Miloses in Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who wrote this?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't tell you, because there are several Miloses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: In his opinion, according to this document, there is a serious danger that members of the Green Berets might launch an attack against the police station in order to obtain weapons. Were there any such plans?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no such plans. This was just an attempt for the weapons of the Territorial Defence to be taken from the people, because the Territorial Defence is the people's defence, so those weapons that belonged to the Territorial Defence belonged to all of us. But the MUP, the Ministry of the Interior, fabricated this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Did any of the weapons belonging to the Territorial Defence end up in, so to speak, Bosniak hands?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the sad truth is that none of the weapons of the former JNA and the Territorial Defence, none of those weapons ended up in the hands of the other peoples, apart from the Serbs. And all of us from 1945 up until 1992 financed the JNA from our own resources.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: You're sure of this.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure of what I have said and what I said earlier on in my testimony. We bought weapons with our own money from soldiers who were returning from Kupres, and we would pay between 1.000 and 2.000 German marks for an automatic rifle. So those are the weapons that ended up in our hands, the ones we paid for.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: With regard to this pledge of loyalty to the police, what was so problematic? What was necessary to sign, what kind of a pledge?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... leaving this document, Your Honours may recall that all documents signed by Milos have been the subject of an allegation, that they're all forgeries. I just want to get clear what the Defence is saying about this document. Is it suggested that on this occasion this document is accurate? Because I'd like to know if that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was asking the witness whether he knew who used that name or that pseudonym, and I also asked him whether what has been alleged in that document corresponds to the way that the Crisis Staff behaved, the Crisis Staff of which the gentleman was a member. I asked nothing else. And in this way, we might have obtained certain information that would have enabled us to assess the validity of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, we are neither here nor there, Ms. Korner, and I think we better leave it at that. Put in a different phraseology, sort of suggesting that he's done all this without prejudice to -- Let's go ahead. You were asking the witness a question with regard to the oath of allegiance or loyalty that -- and your question was, if I recall well, what was so objectionable or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Problematic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, what was problematic about this requirement or request. Yes, Mr. Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as far as I know, I know what was problematic with regard to the other two peoples who refused to serve in that police force. I haven't had access to the oath, and I'm not familiar with the text of the oath, but I know what was contested, what was problematic. These were the marks of the police which was formed by Serbs and Muslims and Croats too at the time. The police had insignia which belonged to Tito's police. They had the five-cornered star. However, all these insignia, all the insignia of Yugoslavia were being removed, and up until that point in time the police force was a Yugoslav police force, because we were -- up until then, we lived in a common state in the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia. But the insignia were removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's already explained this in his previous testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he has.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: And could you tell us, is it common practice for the police to take an oath when they enter service?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. Just like it's common practice for a soldier to take an oath. In my opinion, the police would have to take an oath too. I'm not a policeman, but that's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Defence Exhibit -- Prosecution Exhibit 967.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: It's a diary, the diary of someone whose name is Ilija Buvac.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, the witness has already given evidence about who this man is, so perhaps we can move directly to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: In the diary, the date, the 26th of May. The date has been printed out. In the third paragraph, it says: "As there was no electricity from 1640 hours --" it should probably say "hours," although it's not clear -- "we could not listen to the radio and the television has not been working for several days." Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: The next date is the 27th of May. And the second paragraph says: "During breakfast, Mile Babic, son of Joso," if I see this correctly, "called us on the phone and informed us that there was shooting in Krasulje and he wanted to know about Sveto. He had called him in Velagici --" basically they say that the policeman Milos Kecman was wounded and Dusan Stojakovic, another policeman, was killed. Can you see that? Do you know anything about Kecman and when he was killed?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kecman wasn't killed. He was wounded. Stojakovic was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, did you know that Kecman was wounded?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: The next date is Thursday, the 28th of May. In the lower half, it says: "Around 1800 hours an attack was carried out on Kljuc from the Sarica, Mehmedagica and Sarica Brdo sectors. There were no wounded, no casualties." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says. But when I gave testimony, I said on the day I was taken from the police station at 1800 hours, I can claim for sure that that was not an attack. The people shooting were Serbian soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: The next date, Friday, the 29th, the very first sentence: "Around 0400 hours the hospital in Kljuc was attacked once again." You weren't present then, were you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: The 30th of May, the penultimate paragraph: "Around 1800 hours there was firing around Cuko's house, but it quickly stopped. There was also firing around the Brsac house and around the house of Cedo Acimovic. Ibro Adzamovic from Rejzovici was killed there, although he had not participated in combat." Do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about Ibro's death. I know about these three places where these people had been mentioned, I know that no one else could have fired apart from the Serbian forces, because this is the very centre of Kljuc. Cedo Acimovic's house and the house where Ilija lives and Brsac's house, that's in the very centre of Kljuc. So a member of the armed forces of the Serbian army would have taken an automatic rifle and fired, attacked the Green Berets. They would then say the Green Berets had attacked and they would take a few people to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: The next date we are interested in is Wednesday, the 3rd of June. The last sentence: "Today the electricity was cut off and there was no electricity during the night either." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Thursday, the 4th of June, the second sentence: "Since there is no electricity, the phones are not working. We are getting water from the systems," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Is the question: Do you agree there was no electricity on these dates? Because if so, why didn't you ask it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. We're still waiting for the question, actually, Mr. Trbojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the witness whether these statements about the electricity supply being cut off were correct.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say, because at the time I was in prison in Stara Gradiska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You mentioned the takeover of the repeater, the TV repeater in Kozara.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: My question is: Was the damage to the transmitter on Ravnicki Kamen organised by your Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Did you know about that event?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. All I know is that when this happened, I know that I was happy, because I couldn't watch the second channel of Belgrade television, which to a very large extent contributed to everything that had happened in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Let's return to Mr. Brdjanin. In the first statement you gave - there are four statements - you gave your first statement in Manjaca, and you don't refer to him, you don't mention his name in any context whatsoever; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whose name? Brdjanin's?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I didn't mention him. But in Manjaca, I couldn't even mention myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Vojo Kupresanin.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned Kupresanin because he was there. But I said that I hadn't seen Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: You gave the statement on the 24th of May, 1997 to investigators of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's something else. You should have asked me whether in the course of my stay in Manjaca -- whether it was in the course of my stay or later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: I could show you this, but it's not necessary to waste time.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But we understand each other now. Yes, I gave a statement after the war. And at the time I claimed, and I still claim so today, I claimed that I didn't see Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: You didn't mention him in that statement.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I didn't see him, and I can't lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: You gave a statement on the 17th of May, 1992, and you didn't mention Brdjanin -- 17th of May, 2000 -- and to the Prosecution on the 13th of May, 2001. At that time Mr. Brdjanin was in detention, and you didn't mention him on that occasion either.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, why should I mention him, since I didn't see him?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Is it possible that no one asked about him, no one -- none of the investigators for the Prosecution asked about him?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible. That's possible they didn't ask about him. For example, I remember very well --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: If someone had asked you, you would have said "I have nothing to say about him."

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They asked me whom I had seen and I said I had seen Vojo Kupresanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That brings us to the first break. And with your indulgence -- do you require half an hour or -- 20, 25 minutes would be enough, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm perfectly fine -- I'm prepared, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The idea, Mr. Zecevic, is to try to economise on time so that we could possibly finish by tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. And I'm sure that we will finish by end of tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So 20 to 25 minutes' break. Okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. One -- Your Honour, one thing before I start: The witness has shown that he brought some documents. I assume it's a death certificate and a forensic report which he claims is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have it already, I think, in the -- in the records. No? If I remember well, when Dr. -- what's his name -- was giving evidence here, he gave evidence on the certificate that he was asked to release regarding the death of Omer Filipovic and the other -- if I remember well. I mean, I may be wrong. But I think --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, that was Witness Enis Sabanovic, and in fact he did say that he issued the certificate. But we didn't see it at that time. There was no certificate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if that would be appropriate, but we would like to see the document if the -- from the Prosecutor doesn't object to it. And maybe we can do it while I am conducting the cross-examination. Maybe it can be copied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. I mean, Mr. Filipovic, did you bring over with you a copy of your brother's death certificate or any related -- other related document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I brought a death certificate issued in Banja Luka, and I also brought a record on investigation from 1998 November, when I had my late brother's body exhumed to take it to Kljuc from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps you could make them available, give them to the usher. We'll make copies of them. And when the Prosecution and yourself, Mr. Zecevic, have seen the documents, and ourselves, of course, then you may proceed with putting the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think I have probably misinterpreted the witness, because I believe we have these documents. But I -- in any case, I -- the usher can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think -- I think -- if I remember well, the --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The report we have, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau may be right that we -- the witness was not produced during the evidence -- during the testimony of Sabanovic. However, I think that the death certificate does exist in the records.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The death certificate, but I was thinking about the forensic report. I understood the witness that he has a forensic report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That, I haven't seen, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Which is allegedly forgery. That's what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Filipovic, my name is Slobodan Zecevic, and I am chief counsel of General Talic, and I'm going to ask you several questions. I would like to ask you if we can to keep it brief. I will try and keep my questions brief and allow you to understand with "yes," "no," or "I don't recall," or you don't know, if you don't know anything about it. Could you tell me, Mr. Filipovic, in the former Yugoslavia SFRJ was a multi-ethnic community, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You know in the territory of Serbia proper in Sandzak there are at least 500.000 Muslim who is live there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the number. I don't know the figures. But I do know that they do live there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You told us during your testimony here that you were not satisfied with your status as a nation in that former Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said we were not satisfied with the status that was going to be prepared after the first multi-party elections, but in the former, the old Yugoslavia, we had a very good status.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I recall exactly, you said that in your opinion, you said that Slovenia and Croatia -- you said they were allowed to leave Yugoslavia far too easily. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me if this is really what you thought, that they were allowed far too easily out of Yugoslavia. Why didn't Muslims go to be mobilised and fight for the Yugoslavia of then?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the Muslims did not want to fight other nations in Yugoslavia, because specifically JNA had asked me, to call me to go into the army -- I was captain in reserve -- to fight the Slovenians. I wouldn't have gone because I believed that Slovenians were my people. We were citizens of one state, so why would I go and kill them without any reason? I would have gone -- responded to call-up papers, and 99 per cent of Muslims would have done had we been attacked from the outside, Chinese, Russians, or Americans, it doesn't matter. If we had been attacked from the outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You say without reason. But isn't reason enough? The constitutional role of the army, the JNA's role, was to keep the integrity of the former JNA, of the SFRJ. You as a captain should know that.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but as a captain I also knew that I -- I am not to be dismissed from my duty is the document that I was shown earlier by the gentleman, that I should be dismissed from duty and a Serb be brought in my place. We know that the establishment of the JNA was such that all nations were in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, I'm just going to ask you to focus on answering the question. What you spoke with my learned colleague and the way you answered the questions, that is already in the transcript and we heard it. I asked you whether you're aware that the role of the JNA was to preserve the integrity and indivisibility of the SFRJ.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in the constitution from 1974, yes. But the JNA did not respect the constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did the JNA not respect or did you as members of the Muslim community not respect the constitution?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The JNA did not respect the constitution, because how would they have the right to give helicopters just to one nation, to give weapons just to one nation, while we were all citizens of Yugoslavia and we all contributed to it being built up. We financed it, and we created a respectable armed force in Europe, all of us, Serb, Croats, Slovenes, Muslims, Macedonians, all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So in your opinion, this forced secession or forcible secession which took place first in Slovenia and later was legitimate in fact.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the way that it started, the way the Serbian nationalism started, I believe, yes, that it was legitimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And for that reason you as Muslims, you did not want to respond to call-up papers for mobilisation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, Mr. Filipovic, you spoke that you were not asked about anything in the Kljuc Municipality Assembly as members of the Muslim nation. You said that they were a SDS assembly, that they could have just passed all decision themselves.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For all the decisions that were supposed to be adopted, we were of no importance. We were only needed for the decisions where two-third majority was needed according to the statute. That's when we were needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You were bothered by that because you believed that nobody had the right to make decisions in your name; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, in your opinion isn't that exactly the identical situation as the Serbs had in the Republic Assembly in Sarajevo in the Assembly of the Republic of BH, that is, that they -- they believed that they -- nobody had the right to decide on their fate in their place.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not right. That's not correct. The Serbs had different intentions, contrary to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Because of such a situation, you decided to create the municipality -- or establish the Municipality of Bosanski Kljuc; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This Municipality of Bosanski or Bosnian Kljuc, you established it and the decision was somehow been given a raincheck.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... zero. [Interpretation] This is the official announcement from the press conference that your late brother, Omer Filipovic, gave on the 30th of January, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I may have missed this. What document are we looking at?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Exactly. I'm going to ask --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That explains it because --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 870.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You read this, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see here exactly what I told you, that we asked for the laws of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina to be respected.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The last sentence on page 1, and I'm going to read it. In the Serbian text, at the end of page 1, it says: "It's also been said that this first municipality in Bosnia-Herzegovina, but that its fate depends on the move of the partner, the SDS, because if there is no regionalisation and ethnic basis, then there will be no Municipality of Bosanski Kljuc either." Do you know about such a position?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We wanted nothing to be touched. We wanted the situation to stay as it was, and that we would make everything null and void. But if we had known that the Serbs were preparing for a Serbian Kljuc, if they had wanted to listen to us, we would have called the assembly and we would have then called for the previous situation to be revived.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, you made a decision -- you passed a decision, but then you said if nothing happens with the ethnic the regionalisation, then this decision will have no validity; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He has already given evidence on this, and this is precisely what he has stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But Your Honours, I have asked him whether he is aware of the fact that -- that the -- that the decision which they took concerning the Bosnian Kljuc municipality has been put on hold --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. And he --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And he said I don't -- I don't understand what you mean. That's why I am asking all these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. But he had explained it when he was here before, and he has repeated it today.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That it was put on hold, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But when I ask him -- my first question was: Did you put that decision on hold? He says, "I don't understand."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but he's explained --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is why I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You will agree, Mr. Filipovic, that this position that you had by putting this decision on hold if something changes is identical to the position of the Serb community in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you agree with me or not?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with you because we at our assembly, we didn't threaten that one whole nation would be eradicated, contrary to Karadzic who said publicly in his assembly of his parliament, he said that one whole nation would be eradicated from the face of the earth. We didn't say that in Kljuc. We were just attempting to protect our rights under the constitution, and we said that if Kljuc remains as it was, we have nothing against to be members of the Municipal Assembly of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, I asked you about decisions, not about individual statements. So was your decision identical to that of the Serbian community in BH which said that it wouldn't make Republika Srpska, it wouldn't establish it, if the same situation remained in BH?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Counsel, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, do you think that your position in relation to the establishment of the Bosnian Municipality of Kljuc, was it legitimate? Was it lawful?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was, I believe, the only way to protect our constitutional rights, because in this decision it says that the laws of BH are to be respected, as we saw it earlier. But they were not respected. The laws of BH were not respected.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You mean the laws of BH were not respected in a sense -- in a sense that the SDS which democratic elections got the majority, they managed to get the majority when there was voting in the assembly; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that the tax should go to Sarajevo, that financial means should go to Sarajevo. It means to things going to what they were before and also to the fact that laws were not respected.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, could you tell me, when we are talking about the tax, at that time Bosnia-Herzegovina was still a part of the SFRJ; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, until the referendum in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the former Yugoslavia there was a federal tax, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was federal. There was republic tax. And there was -- there was a local tax.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that from 1991 the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina didn't pay one single dinar into the federal tax that they were supposed to pay, that the tax that was supposed to be collected in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to ask someone who knew about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On several occasions here during your testimony you said that you basically as members of the Muslim nation in Kljuc, you accepted the Community of Municipalities of Banja Luka but not the Autonomous Region of Krajina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor, during your examination-in-chief the Prosecutor showed you a document which was P3 document, and you had to say a lot about this document, had many objections saying that this document wasn't valid because it didn't have a seal, it didn't have a proper number. And this was about the decision of the assembly to become part of the Krajinan Autonomous Region. Do you remember that document?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown P3 and P869 simultaneously, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
