It would be important to know. So there were lots of guards or patrols because of drunken and daft reservists, so to speak, who were coming back from the front, and they were just fooling around.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask you about the sentries or the guards. I asked you about the meeting when you issued instructions for establishment of actual armed formations, platoon companies, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, as far as I was aware, we just said that there would be at Velagici -- that there been a formation, a unit. And then later on each village according to its needs, if they were forced to, then they would do that, because we moved to Velagici at the time when repression started against us and it was in Velagici that we said, "This is where the seat of the Bosnian Kljuc municipality was."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But you went to Velagici in late May; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Officially 25th of May. That was when it actually happened. But there was stuff before then. This was the only location where we could meet where we were not risking our lives and where we were able to meet. And also the Serb authorities in Kljuc let us meet there because they believed that that's how they would keep us in check, that they would keep an eye on us in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I was asking about this meeting, as I said at the very beginning. This meeting was held in late April or in the first couple of days of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether this meeting -- there were cards that were being distributed TO BH -- on the front side there was "TO BH" and on the other side there was a name and surname. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember there was talk of that, but I don't know whether they distributed these cards. I know that there were these cards and it was said they would be distributed. But I know there was talk of that, it did happen, but I don't know whether it actually happened in that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You were already asked by my learned colleague about the instructions that you saw earlier marked with "DB" which was the statement of Alija Delimustafic which was signed, DB95. And because you said that you didn't see the instructions before you were shown it here. Do you know whether your late brother Omer received such a document as a commander or perhaps his deputy Djeric Nerzet?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no. The only document received by fax was the order from the Ministry about Omer being appointed to become a commander. And again, we didn't receive it personally. It first went to Jovo Banjac. All the documents were passed on the phone. And although we know that the phones were being bugged, even our house phones -- and we tried to use official phones. We thought that they were perhaps not being monitored.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it true that in the course of May 1992 you had a fax machine installed in Pudin Han where the staff of the Territorial Defence was?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received a fax machine and the telephone and we set it up, but I don't know whether we had a number for that or not. But we did receive a fax machine and a telephone. My brother and I were stopped by a man in the street as we were going to Velagici, and he said, "Brothers, you're so brave to do this. I was fleeing from you up to now, but the only thing I can do for you to help you is here is this fax that you can have." I can't be sure whether we received the number for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You were asked by the Prosecution who you received orders from. You said that you received orders from Sarajevo because you said that Sarajevo was the only legitimate authority for you.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it happened through the telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I presume that the same thing was valid for all the other municipalities: Sanski Most, Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. You should ask them. I only know things in relation to Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When we're talking about these municipalities, you told us that you met Dr. Mujadzic in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who you met from Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still know him today, Mirzet Karabeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether your late brother as TO commander of Kljuc met Suad Sabic, who was a commander there? Do you know Suad Sabic from Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know him. We're not close.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So he was the commander of the Territorial Defence there, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was something or other, but I don't know what exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, do you know that your late brother also met Midhat Karadzic from Jajce?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are related through the female line. My sister-in-law and Midhat were relatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And Midhat was ...?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the president of Jajce municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Could you tell me, Mr. Filipovic, we spoke about the weapons that you had as the Patriotic League first and then as Territorial Defence of BH. Is it true that you had about 1.000 pieces as --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. I think 7 to 8 hundred in my assessment, but I include in that old-fashioned pistols, hunting rifles, carbine rifles, automatic rifles, anything that would shoot, anything that would fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And 12 to 13 hundred people organised.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I keep saying not so many.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: There were fewer of them.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were fewer of them. Less than 1200. If there had been 1200, things would have gone differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You do know that as the Territorial Defence staff, you also had dynamite and military explosives, plastic explosives? You know that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. We didn't have that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't. If somebody had that, perhaps from their -- in their personal possession. Perhaps they worked in a mine in Majdan or something. But we didn't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Ismet Salihovic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is he a person from that milieu, so to speak? He was a miner, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what he did. I don't know what he did before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether he had Vitezit dynamite?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can I -- how can I know that? How can I know what he had in his own house? It's possible that he had it in his own house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, could you tell us, you as the staff commander of the Patriotic League until your brother was appointed, you certainly had some weapon, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had seven 65-millimetre-calibre handgun, legally owned and paid for 1.000 Deutschmarks, and about 40 bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And nothing else?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that your late brother had a Heckler?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And also Asim Egrlic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Asim Egrlic went to Zagreb to use this money from Switzerland, that he had bought some 30-odd automatic rifles, including that Heckler? One he kept for himself; the other one he gave to Omer.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how he came to possession that, but I know the two of them had 9-millimetre-calibre Hecklers, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Asim Egrlic on that occasion also brought some automatic rifles, Zagi? Do you know them?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you see them?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see them. That's a Croatian production. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Ibrahim Egrlic sold on these Heckler rifles because they were using 9-millimetre-calibre bullets for handguns?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And he reportedly became rich from that.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that. I couldn't claim that. Egrlic was an honest and honourable man. He was much more courageous than his brother Asim, and it is possible that this is out of pure spite that somebody said that about him. He was killed in the war. And I stand by that, that he certainly didn't -- wasn't involved in the sale of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, you as the BH Territorial Defence, did you receive some rifles, AK-47 rifles, from the government in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we received rifles? As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the government bought a large number of these particular type of automatic rifles, AK-47?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Government in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Sarajevo to Kljuc is 225 kilometres. I don't know what they did there. It is possible that they were preparing weapons for self-defence, but I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps read a book by Hasan Efendic called "Who defended Bosnia?"

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... DT26, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Will you be able to conclude on this in two minutes, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Just this document, Your Honour, and then ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the same query. I don't think this is one of our documents, so I'd like to know where it comes from.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I may explain. This is a document which is a part of a book by Mr. Hasan Efendic, and the book is called "Who defended Bosnia?" And this document is -- is an attachment to the book on the -- on page -- just let me find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And this is a copy of one invoice. And I have been able to obtain the translation. If you don't have any -- I will make the reference in a minute, when we find it, and which page it is. But if you don't have any objection, I would like to ask a question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't -- I don't have any -- I don't have any objection, Your Honour. I think -- I'd just like to know a little bit about the context of this though.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: There is a translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I appreciate that. But as to whom this -- how this comes into being, as it were. But for the moment, Your Honour, I'm content if the witness is asked the question, and then we can end for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead with the question, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's -- just for the transcript, it's page 82 of this book, which I -- which I mentioned before. And the book was published in Sarajevo in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, do you see this invoice?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I presume you haven't seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You don't know anything about these rifles; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. I don't know anything about it. But in every war there is a war -- there is weapons being bought, so the government of Sarajevo had to somehow buy weapons in order to defend their citizens, while the Serbs received weapons from the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But this is February 1992.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is February 1992.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in February 1992 the so-called Yugoslav People's Army was already arming Serbs. How can you comment on this saying that there was war in Bosnia and the Serb side had aircraft and helicopters while the government of Sarajevo didn't have anything else but rifles?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I hope that we will agree that there was no war in Bosnia in February 1992, I hope.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no war, but there were spies on both sides and there was preparation for war. So certainly intelligence had found out that they were getting ready, that the war was going to start. And this is the first time that I see this. I hadn't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I will -- I will proceed tomorrow I think another two, two and a half hours. I cannot really be more specific than this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Zecevic. Tomorrow, by the way, the sitting has been moved to the morning. We have a morning session; if I remember well, in Courtroom III. So we'll meet upstairs at 9.00 sharp tomorrow morning. I thank you all. Have a nice afternoon.
